title: Site Sets
appliesTo: how does an extension ship typoscript

hints.text: A site set is how a system extension ships TypoScript. It is a directory Configuration/Sets/<SetName>/ whose config.yaml carries a composer-style name ("typo3/fluid-styled-content"), an optional label, and an optional dependencies list naming other sets by that same name.
Next to config.yaml the set may hold setup.typoscript, settings.definitions.yaml, settings.yaml, labels.xlf, page.tsconfig and route-enhancers.yaml. Only config.yaml is required.

hints: This is how an extension ships TypoScript, and a project's own sitepackage is an extension like any other — the mechanism does not change because the repository is not the core's. Configuring one installation is where it stops being a convention and becomes that site's decision, and this server does not make it.
Its neighbours: site-set-settings for what replaces constants, site-set-labels-and-layouts for what a set declares beside TypoScript, site-set-migration for what the move leaves behind.

title: Site Set Settings Instead of TypoScript Constants

hints.text: settings.definitions.yaml is where a set declares its settings: a categories map and a settings map, each entry with default, type and category. It is the replacement for TypoScript constants — reaching for constants.typoscript in new code is the mistake to avoid here.

A settings value is addressed by its dotted path, and both spellings of it resolve: the set's own settings.yaml writes a nested tree, and the site's config.yaml or a test fixture may hand the same thing over as flat dotted keys — 'my_ext.products.requestPage' => 4 — because SiteSettings flattens a tree into those keys itself and reads either. So the nested form in the set is a convention rather than a requirement.

A site's config/sites/<identifier>/settings.yaml and the settings key inline in its config.yaml are alternatives, not layers: when settings.yaml exists, TYPO3 uses it wholesale and does not merge the inline values into it. Set defaults sit below whichever site-local source wins. The backend settings editor persists to settings.yaml, so keep a site's own values in one place or the first backend save can silently leave inline values behind.

title: Labels and Page Layouts a Site Set Ships

hints.text: The set's labels.xlf resolves to the translation domain <ext>.sets.<setname>; typo3_translation_domain_lookup computes it from the path.
The set's labels.xlf is picked up from the set's own directory and there is no domain to address it by: a label of the set is referenced with its full LLL:EXT: path.

A page layout the set ships in page.tsconfig declares its columns under mod.web_layout.BackendLayouts, and every column needs an explicit `identifier`: that identifier is what the frontend template addresses as {content.<identifier>}. Leaving it out is accepted on the branches that still fall back to a generated one, and the template can then no longer reach its own content — the page renders empty and nothing is logged.

title: What Moving TypoScript Into a Set Leaves Behind
hints: ExtensionManagementUtility::addTypoScriptSetup() and addStaticFile() are the predecessor and are still called from a few sysexts, addTypoScriptSetup with an includeInSiteSets flag that folds the content into the set mechanism. Both mechanisms coexist; new code ships a set.

hints.text: Moving an extension's TypoScript into a set leaves what registered the old static include behind in ext_localconf.php, and nothing reports it. A $GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['FE']['contentRenderingTemplates'] entry naming the removed Configuration/TypoScript/ path can no longer be matched by anything, so it is a cleanup rather than a defect — the content-rendering-templates hint says what reads that key and what a matched entry would have done.
Site set resolution is covered by functional tests under typo3/sysext/core/Tests/Functional/Site/Set/; the labels have their own check, checkIntegritySetLabels.
